entities.name: Independent Agents
entities.rationale: Users group icon at far left of the whiteboard; independent insurance agents who request the single page application. Not inside any container.

entities.name: CloudFront
entities.rationale: Purple icon labeled CLOUDFRONT next to the users; serves the single page application from S3. No container box drawn.

entities.name: S3
entities.rationale: Green bucket icon labeled S3 at the top; hosts the single page application served through CloudFront. No container box drawn.

entities.name: API Gateway
entities.rationale: Purple icon labeled API GATEWAY in the center; entry point for backend calls. No container box drawn.

entities.name: Lambda Authorizer
entities.rationale: Orange Lambda icon at the bottom labeled AUTHORIZER / LAMBDA; Lambda authorizer invoked by API Gateway to validate access. No container box drawn.

entities.name: Lambda
entities.rationale: Orange Lambda icon labeled LAMBDA to the right of API Gateway; serverless Python Lambda with the modernized business logic. No container box drawn.

entities.name: EC2
entities.rationale: Orange icon labeled EC2 at the top right; hosts the legacy Tomcat application still called by the Lambda for non-migrated functions. No container box drawn.

entities.name: DynamoDB
entities.rationale: Blue icon labeled DYNAMODB at the bottom right; regional cache of user information accessed by the Lambda. No container box drawn.

visual_connections.description: Arrow from users to CloudFront: agents request the single page application.
Return arrow from CloudFront back to users: the application is served to the agents.
Curved arrow from S3 down to CloudFront: single page application content served from the S3 bucket through CloudFront.
Arrow from CloudFront to API Gateway: backend calls come into API Gateway.
Curved arrow from API Gateway down to the authorizer Lambda: validates that the caller has access.
Arrow from API Gateway to the Lambda: invokes the serverless Python Lambda.
Double-headed curved arrow between Lambda and EC2: Lambda calls the legacy Tomcat application for non-migrated functions and it calls back down.
Curved arrow from Lambda down to DynamoDB: caching user information.
